title: Two bettors, 500 races: who holds what?
hook: Two bettors, nearly the same belief, the same money. Bet against each other for 500 races.

knows: betting odds are the wealth-weighted average belief (odds-average-the-bettors)
repeated bets multiply your money rather than add to it
doesNotKnow: that repeated betting shifts wealth toward the more accurate bettor, so prices drift toward the truth, though luck can lead for a long time

misconception: Two bettors with similar beliefs will keep similar wealth.
objective: The learner can explain that each race multiplies the ratio of two bettors' money by how well each belief fit the result, so a small edge in accuracy compounds until the accurate bettor holds nearly all the money and the odds approach the truth, even though luck can favour the other bettor for hundreds of races.

claims.text: In this model each race multiplies the ratio of the 60% bettor's money to the 50% bettor's by 1.2 on a win and 0.8 on a loss; three wins and two losses multiply it by 1.11. In run 1 (seed 2211) race 1 is a loss, so the single-race step shows ×0.8.
claims.source: Winners split the pool by stake, so the ratio changes by 0.6/0.5 = 1.2 on a win and 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 on a loss, whatever the shares. 1.2^3 × 0.8^2 = 1.1059. Demo.tsx WIN_X, LOSS_X. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: winners split the pool by stake, so the money ratio changes by 0.6/0.5 = 1.2 on a win and 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 on a loss at any share (node check at a = 0.3 gives 1.2); 1.2^3 x 0.8^2 = 1.10592, shown as 1.11. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 adds the single-race step and its caption/readout. Builder's node replay: seed 2211's first rng() is not under 0.6, so race 1 is a loss; ratio a/(1-a) goes 1.00 -> 0.80. The reveal quotes the recorded first single race. Unverified. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own replay: seed 2211's race 1 is a loss (first rng() >= 0.6). Ratio factor check: for every run and many (from, to) windows, ratio(to)/ratio(from) = 1.2^w × 0.8^l to 1e-6 (0 failures). 1.2^3 × 0.8^2 = 1.1059 -> '1.11'. Reveal quotes the recorded single race (its own run and race number), so other paths stay true. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8: reveal reworded to "by 1.2 on a win, 0.8 on a loss (your race 1: a loss, ×0.8). Three wins and two losses, the true mix, give ×1.11: an edge that compounds". Values unchanged. Needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Derivation: with all-in stakes split by belief and the whole pool shared by winning stake, the ratio a/(1−a) changes by 0.6/0.5 = 1.2 on a win and 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 on a loss at any share. 1.2^3 × 0.8^2 = 1.1059, shown as '×1.11' in the reveal and the Seen row. Own replay: race 1 of seed 2211 is a loss (×0.8); runs 3 to 5 start with a win.

claims.text: The pool's win odds are the money-weighted average belief, so as money moves to the 60% bettor the odds move toward the true 60%.
claims.source: With everyone betting all their money, the share of the pool on 'win' is 0.6·a + 0.5·(1 − a), where a is the 60% bettor's share (Demo.tsx readout). As a → 1 this → 0.6. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: everyone bets everything, so the share of the pool on 'win' is 0.6a + 0.5(1 - a), the readout's formula; it tends to 0.6 as a tends to 1. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8: reveal now "As money moves to the better belief, the pool's odds drift to 60%"; readout label shortened to "Pool odds" (it shows 59.9% / 60.0% at race 500). Needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. The Pool odds readout is (0.6·a + 0.5·(1−a)) × 100, the money-weighted belief; it tends to 60% as a tends to 1. Own replay at race 500: 60.0% (runs 1, 3, 4) and 59.9% (runs 2, 5). The reveal says 'drift to 60%', which fits the claim's 'move toward'; no run reaches above 60%.

recall.question: Two bettors keep betting all their money against each other on the same event. One's belief is slightly closer to the true chance. After a very long time, what is most likely?
options: They stay roughly even, since their beliefs are close
The closer one holds nearly all the money
Whoever is ahead after the first 100 bets stays ahead
recall.why: Each bet multiplies the ratio of their money by how well each belief fit the result. A small edge compounds; luck can lead for a while but not forever.
